title: Lightweight historical backfill mode (avoid full manual re-entry)
description: Wardens are reluctant to type years of paper history into the app tenant-by-tenant, invoice-by-invoice - it's described as boring, slow, and low-value for them. Rather than requiring full ledger reconstruction, offer a fast, minimal way to seed historical context (e.g. a tenant's move-in date and a running balance/opening due, or a bulk CSV import) instead of every past invoice/payment.
acceptanceCriteria: Onboarding an existing (already-resident) tenant supports an optional 'opening balance / dues carried forward' field instead of requiring every past invoice to be re-entered
A bulk import path (e.g. CSV) exists for wardens who do want to bring over structured history, as an alternative to one-by-one manual entry
Skipping historical backfill entirely does not block using the app for new activity going forward

history.note: Added from the v2 feedback session (warden interviews after the v1 field test) and from buried enhancement/limitation notes surfaced while re-reading the full v1 board history.

Explicitly deferred - the opening-balance-vs-reporting-invariant tension flagged in backlog review is real (an opening balance not backed by real invoice/payment rows would drift from what LODGY-22's reports can reconcile) and needs a proper design pass, not a quick call. Will come back to this later; not blocking anything else in the meantime.

Starting - two paths, neither mandatory: an optional dues-carried-forward field at move-in that produces one real opening invoice instead of a re-typed ledger, and a CSV import for wardens who do want structured history.

Two independent backfill paths, both optional. (1) Opening balance: the agreement form gained a 'Dues carried forward (optional)' field with a hint saying plainly that past months need not be re-entered. A non-zero value writes ONE real invoice rather than a number stashed on the agreement, so carried-forward dues flow through the invoice list, reports, reminders and receipts exactly like any other due and can be paid off normally. It is dated the month BEFORE move-in - InvoiceGenerationWorker only ever creates invoices from the current month forward, so that period can never collide with one it generates; a January move-in correctly rolls back to December of the previous year. (2) CSV import: backup/HistoryCsv.kt parses 'phone,month,year,amount_due,amount_paid' - forgiving about blank lines, an optional header and stray spaces, strict about values, and reporting each unreadable line by number instead of dropping it silently, because a warden typing years into a spreadsheet will get some of it wrong and needs to know which lines. More -> Import past history (CSV) shows how many rows are importable, how many carry a phone number no tenant uses, and the first few bad lines before anything is written. Each matched row becomes a real invoice plus, where money was paid, a real payment, with the status derived - so imported history is indistinguishable from history entered at the time. existsForPeriod guards every write, so re-running an import cannot double-bill. AC 3 holds by construction: both paths are opt-in and nothing anywhere requires them. Tests: HistoryCsvTest for the parser (headers, blank lines, bad columns, non-numeric amounts, impossible months/years, negatives, blank phone, empty file); HistoryImportViewModelTest for the matched/unmatched split, unreadable files, PAID/PARTIAL/UNPAID derivation, the re-run guard, and unknown tenants never being written; AgreementFormViewModelTest for the blank, zero, unparseable and January opening-balance cases. testDebugUnitTest green (343 tests).

PASS - all three, including a real CSV import. AC1: the agreement screen has 'Dues carried forward (optional)' with a plain-language hint; entering 3000 for a tenant backdated to 5 Jun 2026 created a single opening invoice (period 5/2026, amountDue 3000, dueDate = move-in) instead of demanding every past month be re-entered. AC2: More > Import past history (CSV) documents the column order and validates before committing - fed it a 4-line file mixing valid rows, an unknown phone and a malformed line, and it reported '2 of 3 row(s) can be imported', '1 row(s) have a phone number no tenant in the app uses - add those tenants first.' and 'Line 4 could not be read: garbage,row,here', then imported exactly the 2 good rows. Verified in the DB: 3/2026 5000 PAID and 4/2026 5000 PARTIAL with a 2000 payment - amounts, statuses and payment rows all correct. AC3: the screen states plainly that skipping changes nothing, and the app worked normally throughout without any backfill.
